'''Anatoly Yakovenko''' (also known as '''Toly Yakovenko''') is a Ukrainian-born software engineer and entrepreneur who co-founded the [[Solana (blockchain platform)|Solana blockchain platform]].

== Early life==
In the early 1990s, Yakovenko moved to the [[United States]] from [[Ukraine]] as a child and learned to program as a teenager.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sraders |first=Anne |last2=Harty |first2=Declan |title=Exclusive: How Anatoly Yakovenko's crypto startup Solana Labs is building what investors think will be a core layer of Web3 |url=https://fortune.com/2022/04/12/solana-anatoly-yakovenko-blockchain-cryptocurrency-ethereum-proof-of-history/ |access-date=2026-01-20 |website=Fortune |language=en}}</ref> He graduated from the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] with a B.S. in computer science.<ref name=":0" />

Yakovenko worked for more than a decade at [[Qualcomm]] as an engineer working on wireless and distributed systems. Since 2016, he has worked as an engineer at Mesosphere, a company that develops software for data centers, and at [[Dropbox]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Events |first=TechCrunch |date=2025-10-17 |title=Crypto’s next chapter with Solana’s Anatoly Yakovenko at Disrupt 2025 |url=https://techcrunch.com/2025/10/17/cryptos-next-chapter-with-solanas-anatoly-yakovenko-at-techcrunch-disrupt-2025/ |access-date=2026-01-20 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="ForbesUA-2021-12-14" />

== Career ==
=== Solana ===
{{main|Solana (blockchain platform)}}

In 2017, Yakovenko began outlining an approach he later described as ''proof of history (PoH)'', a method intended to create an ordered record of events to support faster consensus on a blockchain network.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mathews |first=Jessica |title=Will Solana become the base layer of Web3? |url=https://fortune.com/2022/04/13/solana-base-layer-blockchain-web3/ |access-date=2026-01-20 |website=Fortune |language=en}}</ref> Yakovenko sought to address the [[blockchain trilemma]] of throughput, decentralization, and security by combining a ''[[proof of stake]]'' (PoS) design with a mechanism he called ''proof of history''. He described PoH as assigning timestamps within the network so validators spend less time establishing the timing and ordering of transactions, enabling faster "time consensus" while maintaining a decentralized validation process.<ref name="ForbesUA-2021-12-14">{{cite news |last=Antoniuk |first=Daryna |date=December 14, 2021 |title=A Ukrainian, Anatoly Yakovenko, is building the world's fastest blockchain. How investors made more than $1 billion from his Solana startup. |url=https://forbes.ua/innovations/ukrainets-anatoliy-yakovenko-stvoryue-nayshvidshiy-u-sviti-blokcheyn-yak-investori-zarobili-na-startapi-1-mlrd-14122021-2973 |access-date=January 20, 2026 |work=Forbes Ukraine}}</ref> He went on to co-found Solana Labs with other engineers, and the project was later renamed ''Solana'' after an earlier name conflicted with another blockchain project.<ref name="Fortune20222">{{cite news |last1=Sraders |first1=Anne |last2=Harty |first2=Declan |date=April 14, 2022 |title=The Ukrainian-born engineer behind Solana Labs learned to code as a teen and had a 'lightbulb' moment about the blockchain |url=https://fortune.com/2022/04/14/who-is-anatoly-yakovenko-solana-labs-building-web3/ |access-date=January 20, 2026 |work=Fortune}}</ref><ref name="TechCrunch2021">{{cite news |last=Loizos |first=Connie |date=May 14, 2021 |title=Solana, a blockchain platform followed by top crypto investors, says it's far faster than Ethereum |url=https://techcrunch.com/2021/05/14/solana-a-blockchain-platform-followed-by-top-crypto-investors-says-its-a-lot-faster-than-ethereum/ |access-date=January 20, 2026 |work=TechCrunch}}</ref>

In 2022, a putative class action filed in the [[United States District Court for the Northern District of California|U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California]] named Yakovenko and Kyle Samani, alleging violations connected to token-related offerings and disclosure. In 2024 the court denied defendants' motion to compel arbitration and noted that plaintiffs had voluntarily dismissed, without prejudice, their claims against Yakovenko and the Solana Foundation; the case proceeded against remaining defendants.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Miller |first=Rosemarie |title=New Lawsuit Alleging That Solana Is A Security Could Have Big Implications For The Crypto Investment Landscape |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/rosemariemiller/2022/07/07/new-lawsuit-alleging-that-solana-is-a-security-could-have-big-implications-for-the-crypto-investment-landscape/ |access-date=2026-01-20 |work=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>
